attributes.axis_log: FIX1 (committed 1ab025a02) camera.c:2368 -- target emits `fcmpo f2,f1; ble` (source form `nearestDistance > blendThreshold`) where ours emitted `fcmpo f1,f3; bge` (source form `blendThreshold < nearestDistance`). These are the algebraically equivalent swapped-operand forms; respelling the relational operator to match target's operand order made the branch polarity exact and removed both the ble/bge token pair and a neighbouring cluster. FIX2 (committed 5bec8c5da) camera.c:2344-2363 -- the three symmetric trigger-selection arms each emitted as target `stw <global>=index; fmr <threshold>=candidate; addi count++; lfs +0x18; lfs +0x14` while our source ordered them count++, lfs, lfs, threshold, global, i.e. very nearly reversed. Reordering all three arms' statements to target's emission order removed all three repeated 4-instruction misalignments at once. NOTE both fixes measured NEUTRAL on `real` and on `lines`; `real` stayed pinned at 266 throughout because the residual register permutation keeps those same lines differing even once they are correctly ALIGNED. Only the --ops cluster list and objdiff fuzzy exposed the gain.
attributes.conclusion_for_next_agent: The 2026-08-30 record's premise 'opcode multiset already matches' was NO LONGER TRUE when re-measured (4 tokens differed), which is exactly why the REVERIFY banner matters -- the capped register-permutation diagnosis was sound but it was masking two ordinary source-reachable structural bugs sitting on top of it. The register permutation itself is untouched and remains capped on the prologue r4/r5 dead-register-reuse axis. Next cheapest leads: the three type-slot load reorders at fn+0xd4-0xf4 (lwz/lfs/lfd trio) and the fn+0x1e4 arm, which is the fourth, larger selection arm and was NOT covered by FIX2.
